elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... at the end of any calendar month" — covers both the Agreement and the order-level attachments (Service Option Attachments are the Order Form-referenced attachments).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 3.4(a) requires "at least one month's prior written notice" and 3.4 makes termination effective only "at the end of any calendar month", so the exit can take materially longer than 30 days from notice; the redline does not change either the one-month period or the calendar-month-end anchor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears in the rendered clause; 3.4 addresses only notice and early termination charges. To meet this element the drafter must insert an express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only Agreement-level termination right is for uncured material breach (3.3); its only unilateral exit is non-renewal effective at the end of the then-current term (3.2). No mid-term IBM convenience right exists.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 3.4(a) requires only "at least one month's prior written notice" — a shorter, more Customer-favourable notice burden that sits inside the 60–90 day fallback ceiling.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Redline to 3.4(b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, not to exceed three (3) months' charges." (Basis of the three months' charges is left unspecified — see reasons.)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: IBM has no convenience right at all; 3.2 permits IBM only to prevent auto-renewal by notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term", with the termination expressly effective at term end, and 3.3 is breach-only. The mapping's quote of the material-breach clause is the wrong support, but the element is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 3.2 requires notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; IBM otherwise has no convenience exit, so no shorter-notice Vendor convenience right exists.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Customer keeps a one-month convenience exit (better than 60–90 days), IBM has no mid-term convenience right, IBM's only unilateral exit is term-end non-renewal on 90 days' notice, and the added cap closes the only genuine gap (open-ended Attachment A early termination charges).

Preferred level fails on two elements: there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges after Customer's convenience termination, and the exit is anchored to the end of a calendar month after one month's notice rather than a flat 30 days.

Minimality fails: relocating "for convenience" from the end of the sentence to immediately after "this Agreement" was not required by any selected fallback element — the original wording already carried the qualifier for both the Agreement and any Service Option Attachment. This is a cosmetic move of words outside the target element (the ETC cap).

The relocation also degrades the drafting: as rendered, "for convenience" now sits before the parenthetical and reads as qualifying only the Agreement branch, leaving the "or any Service Option Attachment" branch without the qualifier. If the drafter wants to keep this edit, revert the move or repeat the qualifier in the Service Option Attachment branch.

Intent is preserved on the substance: the calendar-month-end effective date, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out, the Attachment A charge cross-reference, and IBM's 3.3 forfeiture of early termination charges on its own breach all survive without contradiction.

Tighten the cap's basis in operative language: "not to exceed three (3) months' charges" should specify three months of the recurring charges for the terminated Service Option Attachment(s) (or for the Agreement, as applicable), otherwise the cap amount is arguable at exit.
Note (not a redline): the absence of a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges is a preferred-position gap only and is correctly flagged in the rationale rather than pursued.
